resources.string: Keeps Faro running so it can check this device\'s screen and tell the member\'s allies if monitoring stops. Nothing runs in the background that the member has not agreed to.
The notice that this device is monitored by Faro. It stays while Faro runs.
Important notices from Faro, such as who your allies are.
This device is monitored by Faro. Screenshots are blurred and shared with your allies.
Faro is not set up on this device yet. It monitors nothing.
Faro is working on this phone. There is nothing to do.
Faro couldn\'t start on this phone. Restart the phone. If it still says so, tell whoever runs your instance.
There is a notice from Faro you have not read.
This screen only shows what Faro is doing. Nothing here can stop, pause or hide monitoring.
Notifications are off for Faro, so the notice that this phone is monitored can\'t be shown. Your allies are not told, but turn them on.
Accessibility is off for Faro, so Faro can\'t see the screen, and your allies are told. Open Accessibility settings, choose Faro and switch it on.
Device protection is off, so Faro can be uninstalled without a warning to your allies first. Turn it on.
Battery saving is on for Faro, so Android may stop it. Your allies are told if it does. Choose Don\'t optimize for Faro.

Faro helps someone stay accountable about what they look at on their devices. Screenshots are blurred on this phone before anything leaves it, and only the member\'s chosen allies can open them. Your Faro instance can\'t read them.\n\nThis phone is monitored for as long as Faro is installed. Removing Faro is allowed, but it is never silent: your allies are told.
Open the Computers page of your Faro web app, add a device and copy the link. Paste it here. If you only have the address of your instance, paste that and type the code the web app shows.
With a Faro address, also type the code the web app shows next to it.
This phone will be monitored by Faro for as long as it is enrolled, and your allies will be told if that stops. The instance is at %1$s.
The member key in the link: %1$s
Waiting for approval in the web app
Open the Computers page of your Faro web app and check that this code matches, then approve the device. Monitoring starts then.
The device was refused in the web app. Faro monitors nothing on this phone. To try again, create a new enrollment link.
One more thing: Faro needs a few permissions to do its job.
Android shows a notice for as long as Faro runs. It says that this phone is monitored. Faro needs permission to show it.

Faro uses Android\'s Accessibility service to take screenshots and to see which app or website is in front. Open Accessibility settings, choose Faro (under Installed apps or Downloaded apps) and switch it on.\n\nFaro doesn\'t come from the Play Store, so Android 13 and later may grey the switch out and say it is a restricted setting. To allow it: tap Open app info below, tap the three-dot menu at the top right, choose Allow restricted settings and confirm. The menu only appears after you have tried to switch Faro on once. Then come back and switch it on.
Faro becomes a device administrator so that removing Faro is never silent: before it can be uninstalled, your allies are told. It can\'t lock, wipe or change anything on this phone.
Faro can then tell your allies before it is uninstalled. It asks for no other control of this phone.
Android can stop apps that run all the time to save battery. Faro has to keep running. Choose Allow on the next screen.
Everything Faro needs is on. You can close this. The Faro notice stays at the top of the screen while it runs.
Lets Faro take blurred screenshots and see which app or website is in front, for the accountability partners of the member who enrolled this phone. The member agreed to this, and it is never hidden.
Turning this off lets Faro be removed. Your allies are told that you are doing it, right now.
